subtitulo: Softening a food opinion so it doesn't offend
descripcion: English speakers soften opinions far more than Spanish speakers do. *That's wrong* is grammatically perfect and lands as rude; *I'm not sure that's right* says the same thing and keeps the conversation going. This is not politeness for its own sake: a softened claim is easier to defend, because you have not committed to more than you can support.

filas: A bit heavy, don't you think?
cuadroReferencia.notaPie: One or two per opinion. Three or more and it stops sounding careful and starts sounding evasive.

ejemplos.texto: *It's a bit rich for me, but that might just be my taste.*
*I'd say it needs a little more salt.*
*It's not really what I expected, to be honest.*

notas: *A bit* before a negative adjective is the single most useful softener in spoken English: *a bit dry*, *a bit late*, *a bit expensive*.
*To be honest* and *to be fair* soften rather than emphasise, which surprises learners.
Never soften a fact. *The restaurant might close at eleven* when you know it does sounds evasive rather than careful.

es.en: A plain Spanish opinion (eso es un error) translated literally (that's a mistake) often sounds harsher in English than intended. Adding a softener (I think that might be a mistake) brings it to the intended level.
es.es: Una opinión directa en español («eso es un error») traducida literalmente («that's a mistake») suele sonar más dura en inglés de lo que se pretende. Añadir un atenuante («I think that might be a mistake») la lleva al nivel adecuado.

de.en: German softens with particles (das ist wohl nicht ganz richtig), which disappear in translation and leave that's wrong. English needs a lexical softener: I'm not sure that's quite right.
de.de: Im Deutschen wird mit Partikeln abgeschwächt («das ist wohl nicht ganz richtig»). Bei der Übersetzung verschwinden diese leicht und übrig bleibt «that's wrong». Englisch braucht stattdessen eine lexikalische Abschwächung: «I'm not sure that's quite right».

it.en: A plain Italian statement (è sbagliato) becomes that's wrong, which sounds harsh in English. A softener (I'm not sure that's quite right) brings it to the intended level.
it.it: Un'affermazione italiana diretta («è sbagliato») diventa «that's wrong», che suona duro in inglese. Un attenuatore («I'm not sure that's quite right») riporta il tono al livello desiderato.

fr.en: C'est faux becomes that's false or that's wrong, which sounds harsh in English. A softener (I'm not sure that's quite right) brings it to the intended level.
fr.fr: «C'est faux» devient «that's false» ou «that's wrong», formulations dures en anglais. Un atténuateur («I'm not sure that's quite right») ramène le ton au niveau voulu.

pt.en: Isso está errado becomes that's wrong, which sounds harsh in English. A softener (I'm not sure that's quite right) brings it to the intended level.
pt.pt: «Isso está errado» vira «that's wrong», que soa duro em inglês. Um atenuante («I'm not sure that's quite right») leva a frase ao tom desejado.

errores: Saying nothing at all instead of disagreeing, which is the opposite over-correction.
Stacking: *I think maybe it could possibly be a bit…*
Softening a fact or a number.
*I'm not agree* — the fossilised error worth naming once.

es: *Igual no viene* rendered as *Equal he doesn't come* instead of *He might not come*.
de: *eigentlich* rendered as *actually* in every sentence, which sounds like a constant correction.
it: *Diciamo* carried over as *Let's say* in every sentence until it becomes a tic.
fr: *Disons que* carried over as *Let's say that* in every sentence until it becomes a tic.
pt: *Mais ou menos* carried over as *More or less* for every hedge.

traducciones.it: la data di scadenza / termine minimo di conservazione

redemittel.expresion: It might just be my taste.

traducciones.de: Vielleicht liegt es nur an meinem Geschmack.
traducciones.fr: C’est peut-être juste une question de goût.
traducciones.it: Forse è solo una questione di gusti.
traducciones.pt: Talvez seja apenas uma questão de gosto.

traducciones.es: no estoy seguro de que sea así
traducciones.de: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, ob das stimmt.
traducciones.fr: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit juste.
traducciones.it: Non sono sicuro che sia corretto.
traducciones.pt: Não tenho a certeza de que isso esteja certo.

mision.consigna: Give honest feedback on a dish a friend cooked for you that you didn't really like.
requisitos: one *It might just be my taste*

microtareas.texto: Write three blunt opinions about food, then soften each one.
Change *That's wrong* to five softer versions.
Record 90 seconds on a dish you don't like, softened throughout.

autochequeo: Any opinion with three or more stacked?
Did I soften a fact by mistake?
Would a British listener find any sentence blunt?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on hedging and softening. (1) Mark each softener and say whether it fits. (2) Mark every flat opinion that an English speaker would have softened. (3) Flag any stacking. (4) Flag any fact I softened by mistake. Do not correct anything else.
